body.p: Claims 1-19 are now pending in this application. Claims 1, 7, and 16 have been amended. Favorable consideration and allowance of this application is respectfully requested in light of the following amendments and remarks.
I. Drawings Objection
The Drawings stand objected to under 37 CFR 1.83(a) for failing to show every feature of the invention specified in the claims. In particular, the Examiner contends that the limitations of claims
11, 12, 13, and 15 regarding how the claimed surfaces and axis are arranged must be shown. See Office Action, p. 2.

Applicant refers the Examiner to FIG. 1 of the as-filed application, which is provided below. FIG. 1 clearly illustrates the orientation of antenna arrays 104 and satellites 101 with respect to each other.
Ica
In light of the above, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the objection to the Drawings.
II. Claim Rejection - 35 U.S.C. §112(b)

Claim 7 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. §112(b) for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention. Specifically, the Examiner contends that the recitation "obtained sensor" at the end of claim 7 is not understood. See Office Action, p .3. Applicant has amended claim

7 as suggested by the Examiner. In particular, "obtained sensor" has been amended to "obtained sensor data". As a result, Applicant respectfully request withdrawal of the rejection of claim 7 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b).
III. Claim Rejection - 35 U.S.C. §103

Claims 1, 3-7, 14-16, and 18-19 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over "Spacecraft Formation Flying System Design and Controls for Four Nanosats Mission" by Song et al. ("Song") in view of WIPO Publication 1993/009029 to Stuart et al. ("Stuart"). Claim 2 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Song in view of Stuart and further in view of WIPO Publication 2018/037424 to Satak et al. ("Satak"). Claim 9 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Song in view of Stuart and Satak and further in view of U.S. Patent No. 8,334,809 to Nichols et al. ("Nichols"). Claims 10-13 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Song in view of Stuart and further in view of Nichols. Claim 8 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Song in view of Stuart and further in view of U.S. Publication No. 2018/02514240 to Rettman et al. ("Rettman"). Claim 17 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Song in view of Stuart and further in view of Russian Patent No. 2668378 to Viktorovich et al. ("Viktorovich").

Applicant has amended independent claims 1 and 16 to further distinguish the present invention from the cited art. Independent claim 1 has been amended to define a satellite system comprising a control system configured to dynamically change the configuration and shape of the formation by controlling the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the set for improved tracking capabilities in that the antenna array of at least one of the satellites in the satellite formation thereby can be adapted to the movement patterns of the object whose observation data is currently collected by at least one of the satellites in the formation.

Similarly, independent claim 16 has been amended to define a method including the step of controlling, by the control system, the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the set at least partly based on said received observation data for dynamically changing the configuration and shape of the formation for improved tracking capabilities in that the combination of satellites in the satellite formation is thereby adapted to the movement patterns of the object whose observation data is currently collected by at least one of the satellites in the formation.
Support for the above amendments can be found on page 10, line 10 to page 11, line 4 of the as-filed application.

Song describes a satellite formation with four nanosats where the relative distance between the nanosats can be decreased and increased during along-track and cross-track formations, respectively, via orbit controls in the desired duration. Song further describes a formation flying earth observation mission that targets the studying of physical phenomena, including "electron microbursts, plasma trough, electron density and temperature, length of coherence for bubbles/blobs, and electromagnetic ion cyclotron waves" and does not require any antennas, which is obvious from FIG. 7 of Song.
In Song, the driving motivation of the formation flying system is to avoid that the

nanosats "pass the same point at different times and be located at different longitude points on the same latitude", see for example the abstract of Song. In contrast to Song, the present invention is based on the idea that antenna elements on multiple satellites are virtually aggregated together to form a single large antenna array, and hence requiring a formation flying system to satisfy the requirements of missions that use distributed antennas on multiple satellites to form a single large aggregated virtual aperture for certain applications.

The problem addressed in Song is that nanosats that move along similar orbital planes drift apart owing to the difference in orbital drift rate. The drift recovery control can be performed several times because of thrust limitations and control errors. The formation flying system in Song shall maintain the relative distance to prevent the nanosats from passing through each other, see for example column 1 on pages 151 and 152, and the text to Fig. 4.

FIG. 1 of Stuart discloses a spacecraft designs for a Satellite Communication System including a hemispherical, high-gain, electronically-steered antenna array (12) that is always pointed toward the Earth (E) and where the interior of the dome-shaped antenna array (12) is used to store solar cell panels (16) which unfurl through an opening (15) in the space-facing array (18) when the spacecraft (10) reaches its final orbit.

Furthermore, Song and Stuart are dealing with two different types of missions, where Song is directed to handling close formations requiring autonomous control and hence mutual communications for control purposes whereas Stuart describes a constellation of satellites that are loosely coupled with large distances apart. In contrast to the systems disclosed in the Song and Stuart references, the antennas in the satellite formation of the present invention are arranged for collecting observation data (i.e., are not cover segments for protecting solar panels enclosed behind the array of cover segments) and are further arranged for communications between the satellites in the formation, where at least one of satellite is capable of transmitting observation data to earth.

FIG. 4 of Satak illustrates an exemplary architecture of a space internet network. The space internet network comprises a Satellite Constellation 401, a plurality of Earth Internet Gateways 402a... 402n and a plurality of User Terminals 403a, 403b, 403c... 403n. The Satellite Constellation 401 comprises a plurality of satellites 401a, 401b... 401n. The Satellite Constellation 401 forms a network in space, that enables a communication between the plurality of satellites 401a, 401b ... 401n and the plurality of Earth Internet Gateways 402a ... 402n.

Independent claim 1, as amended, distinguishes over Song, and Song in combination with any and all of the other references (e.g., Stuart, Satak and Nichols) cited in the Non-Final Office Action, by defining a satellite system comprising a control system that is configured to dynamically change the configuration and shape of the satellite formation by controlling the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the set for improved tracking capabilities in that the antenna array of at least one of the satellites in the satellite formation thereby can be adapted to the movement patterns of the object whose observation data is currently collected by at least one of the satellites in the formation.

Independent claim 16, as amended, distinguishes over Song, and Song in combination with any and all of the other references (e.g., Stuart, Satak and Nichols) cited in the Non-Final Office Action, by defining a method for dynamically controlling the configuration and shape of a satellite formation of a satellite system that includes the step of controlling, by the control

body.p: In light of the above, Applicant contends that amended independent claims 1 and 16 are patentably distinct from the cited prior art. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejection of independent claims 1 and 16 under 35 U.S.C. §102(a), along with all claims depending therefrom.
In light of the amendments and remarks above, Applicant believes the application is in condition for allowance.
